token.explanation: A small piece of text, such as a word, part of a word or a punctuation mark. The model reads and writes text as a sequence of tokens.

attention.explanation: The step where each token gathers information from earlier tokens, weighing some of them more than others.

embedding.explanation: A long list of numbers that stands for a token. Similar tokens get similar lists.

layer.explanation: One of the repeated transformer blocks that the numbers pass through, one after another.

head.explanation: One of several attention units inside a layer. They work side by side, and each can focus on different relationships between tokens.

mlp.explanation: The feed-forward part of each block. It reshapes each token's numbers on its own, without looking at other tokens.

logit.explanation: The raw score the model gives each possible next token, before the scores are turned into probabilities.

probability-distribution.explanation: A list of chances, one for every possible next token, that add up to 100%.

prefill.explanation: Processing all the tokens of the input text in one pass, before the first new token is generated.

decode.explanation: Generating one new token, reusing what was already computed for the earlier tokens.

flops.explanation: Floating-point operations: a count of the additions and multiplications a computation needs.

kv-cache.explanation: Memory that keeps the keys and values of earlier tokens, so they do not have to be computed again for each new token.
